reviewer: Captain (provenance resolution between two committed records; not a counsel approval)
question: The specification's statutoryAuthority section is unbound because two committed records disagree about which ORS subsection governs the dismissed-charge and acquittal branches. Which record controls, and does the disagreement survive?
finding: It does not survive. The disagreement is between a review and a later reading of the enrolled session laws that supersedes it, and the enrolled reading answers the question: ORS 137.225(1)(d) governs dismissals and acquittals, ORS 137.225(1)(c) governs the no-accusatory-instrument branch. The memo's attribution is correct and the review's is superseded.

theTrapThisRecordExists.what: data/record-clearing/legal-design-intake/OR.memo.json and the Edition 1.2 legal review disagree in a way that reads, on a first pass, as the review being right.
theTrapThisRecordExists.reviewSays: OR__LEGAL-REVIEW__STATEWIDE__oregon-record-clearing-legal-review__ASOF-2026-08-01__EN.md files Track 1 (arrest, no charges), Track 2 (dismissed charge) AND Track 3 (acquittal) all under ORS 137.225(1)(c), and files subsection (1)(d) relief separately as Track 7, 'Unidentified / Additional research required'.
theTrapThisRecordExists.memoSays: or_arrest_no_charges is (1)(c); or_dismissed_charge and or_acquittal are (1)(d).
theTrapThisRecordExists.whyTheReviewLooksAuthoritative: The memo's own `_controllingReview` field names that review as the controlling review source, checksum-verified. Read only that far and the review appears to win, which would make the route key naming (1)(c) correct for all three branches and dissolve the split recorded on 2026-09-19.
theTrapThisRecordExists.whyItDoesNot: The same memo carries `_officialAuthorityConfirmation`, recording that the review's readiness record required an official-authority refresh, that the review's own primary authority was a Justia compilation and oregon.public.law, and that the enrolled session laws were then read at the Oregon Legislature's own channel on 2026-08-06. The memo is the later record and rests on the better source. Its own words: 'the position changed materially'.
theTrapThisRecordExists.instruction: Do not act on the review's (1)(c) attribution for the dismissed-charge or acquittal branches. It is superseded. This record exists so the next reader who greps the review does not repeat the mistake.

whatTheEnrolledReadingEstablished.instrument: HB 2492, enacted as Oregon Laws 2025 chapter 349, approved 2025-06-20, effective 2026-01-01, applying to motions filed on or after that date, amending ORS 137.225 as previously amended by section 55, chapter 70, Oregon Laws 2024.

subsectionIdentity.quote: ORS 137.225(1)(d) makes acquittals and dismissals available at any time, subsection (9) states in terms that "There is no time limit for making an application", and no provision forcing a dismissed serious charge to wait a conviction period appears anywhere in the enacted section. Subsection (1)(d) itself is identified, closing the review's Track 7 blocker.
subsectionIdentity.consequence: The review's single most important open question -- whether a dismissed serious charge must wait the conviction period -- is answered, and (1)(d) is no longer unidentified relief. Track 7 and Tracks 2/3 were the same subsection all along.

objectionPeriod.quote: the prosecuting attorney has 120 days from filing to object under ORS 137.225(2)(a), which answers the review's open question on the objection period
objectionPeriod.consequence: The OJD packet's 'The District Attorney typically has 120 days to object' now has a statutory basis. The packet's hedge 'typically' need no longer be the only thing a participant is told.

fees.quote: no court filing fee under ORS 137.225(1)(g), the prosecuting attorney may not charge a fee under ORS 137.225(2)(e), and where the Department of State Police performs only one record check it may charge only one fee regardless of how many counties the person files in
fees.consequence: The 'No Filing Fee' printed on the OJD caption has a statutory basis. The review's secondary-source figure of 'about $33 per conviction' is not adopted and is not printed: it came from a Collateral Consequences Resource Center profile, not from the enrolled text.

grantStandard.quote: under ORS 137.225(3)(b) the court shall grant a motion under (1)(c) or (1)(d), and shall grant a motion under (1)(a) where no objection is received, and under ORS 137.225(3)(a) even on an objection the court shall grant unless it makes written findings by clear and convincing evidence that the person's circumstances and behaviour create a risk to public safety

sealingEffect.reviewText: under ORS 137.225(8)(b) the arrest, citation, charge or conviction is **deemed not to have occurred**, so the person may lawfully deny it on most applications.
sealingEffect.bearingOnTheOpenCitationQuestion: The 2026-09-20 form record noted that the OJD instructions attribute that effect to 'ORS 137.255(4)', which is a different statute. The review independently places the effect at ORS 137.225(8)(b). Two sources now point away from the form's citation. That strengthens the observation but does not close it: this record still does not print a subsection for the sealing effect, because the enrolled reading above did not address it and a participant-facing citation should rest on the enacted text rather than on two documents agreeing that a third is wrong.
sealingEffect.reviewTextNote: The review is a markdown document and its emphasis markers are preserved in this quote rather than silently dropped; the emphasised phrase is 'deemed not to have occurred'.

vehicleConfirmedIndependently.quote: The form build blocker is closed twice over: ORS 137.225(12) requires the State Court Administrator to create statewide motion and proposed-order forms, and Edition 1.2 retains the Oregon Judicial Department Criminal Set-Aside (Adult Cases) packet at REV-2026-01, matching the effective date ... The review's statement that no Oregon forms were supplied and that no statewide form was confirmed is therefore superseded, and every filing track moves from the review's provisional custom_pleading to official_pdf_fill.
vehicleConfirmedIndependently.why: That record reached official_pdf_fill by reading the form itself and finding one instrument with a check-one-option Eligibility Statement covering every branch. This reaches it from the statute, which requires the statewide forms to exist. Two independent routes to the same answer, and the review's 'a custom pleading may legally be used' is not a licence to prefer one now that the official form exists.

proposedOrderGap.statute: ORS 137.225(12) requires statewide motion AND proposed-order forms.
proposedOrderGap.observed: The OJD Criminal Set-Aside (Adult Cases) packet at REV-2026-01 is five pages -- three instruction pages, then Motion and Declaration pages 1-2. It contains no proposed order, and the Oregon source library holds no proposed-order form: 02_PACKET_FORMS carries only this packet and the marijuana motion.
proposedOrderGap.alsoObserved: The packet-set manifest declares a proposed-order component (or_acquittal-proposed-order-2), and the memo's filing rule for all three branches says 'File the motion and proposed order'.
proposedOrderGap.disposition: Open. A required statewide form that the corpus does not hold is a source gap, not a licence to draft one: the Form vs Custom Pleading rule says an official form controls where one exists, and ORS 137.225(12) says this one is supposed to exist. Acquire the OJD proposed-order form before deciding whether any custom proposed order is appropriate. Not resolved here and not drafted here.

effectOnThePriorRecord.outcome: Confirmed, not corrected. That record read or_acquittal as a (1)(d) branch and the route key as naming (1)(c), and concluded the route spans two statutory situations and must be split. The enrolled reading confirms the subsection identities it relied on. The split stands on a firmer basis than the memo alone.
effectOnThePriorRecord.refinement: Its comparison table recorded the timing precondition for the (1)(d) branches as 'no waiting period'. The enrolled text is stronger and should be used instead: subsection (9), 'There is no time limit for making an application'.

whatIsNowAvailableToBind.note: Six of the specification's seven unbound sections now have an authority, between this record and the form record. They are NOT bound by this record; binding happens in the specification when the route split lands, so the specification and the route model move together.

sections.filingDestination: OJD instructions page 3 of 3: file in the circuit court where the case happened or would have happened. Branch-invariant.
sections.feeAndWaiver: ORS 137.225(1)(g) no court filing fee; ORS 137.225(2)(e) the prosecuting attorney may not charge; one State Police record check means one fee across counties. The OJD caption prints 'No Filing Fee'.
sections.serviceAndNotice: The review states service on the office of the prosecuting attorney who prosecuted the matter, or who had authority to prosecute if no accusatory instrument was filed, with a full set of fingerprints, and the OJD packet carries the Certificate of Mailing on the instrument itself.
sections.copyRequirements: OJD instructions page 3 of 3, step 3: two copies, one for the participant's records and one for the District Attorney. The packet does not state a court copy count.
sections.hearingAndObjectionStops: ORS 137.225(2)(a), 120 days from filing to object; OJD instructions describe a hearing being scheduled on objection.
sections.postFilingTimeline: OJD instructions steps 1-6 and 'What happens next?', with the grant standard at ORS 137.225(3)(a)-(b).

whatIsNowAvailableToBind.stillUnbound: statutoryAuthority. Not because the subsections are unknown -- they are now known per branch -- but because this one runtime route still stands in for more than one of them. It binds when the split lands and each route carries its own subsection.

notResolvedHere.sameEpisodeRule: The memo records that ORS 137.225(7)(a)(B) as enacted disqualifies a person convicted of any other offence within the look-back period 'whether or not the other conviction is for conduct associated with the same criminal episode', while the OJD packet describes the carve-out as 'traffic violations or a single violation offense' without mentioning same-episode convictions. The memo adopts neither reading and makes no eligibility statement where a same-episode conviction is in play. That position is preserved here unchanged.
notResolvedHere.marijuanaTrack: ORS 475C.397's text is not published in the enrolled session laws that were read and only commercial compilations carry it, so the marijuana track stays deferred. That is the standing reason OR:marijuana-specific-set-aside-redesignation is incomplete.
notResolvedHere.monetaryObligations: The 2025 monetary-obligations relief is narrower than the review described, keyed to pre-July-1-2015 municipal or justice court marijuana-possession judgments under one ounce. Not applied generally.

remainingReview: Counsel review of the branch split and of every statutory reading relied on here. This record resolves which committed record controls; it does not substitute for counsel reading ORS 137.225 as amended by Oregon Laws 2025 chapter 349. The proposed-order form gap and the same-episode rule both remain open.
